**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Assignment and change of control**

The agreement's assignment provision (§ 20(d)) is a flat mutual prohibition: neither party may assign without the other's written consent, with no affiliate carve-out, no M&A successor carve-out, and no reasonableness standard. That is squarely in the playbook's walk-away zone for us as customer. It is reinforced by § 3(c) (Sparkling shall "not assign this Agreement… except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing") and the "non-transferable" licence grant in § 2 — meaning an internal reorganisation or sale of the business could strand us without the software.

On the positive side, Garman has **no** change-of-control termination or re-pricing right: § 17 termination triggers are limited to Sparkling's convenience right, insolvency events and breach, and the phrase "change of control" appears nowhere in the document.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):**
- § 20(d): permits Sparkling to assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets/shares; confirms no such transaction or change of control is a breach or gives Garman any termination, suspension or re-pricing right; adds "not unreasonably withheld or delayed" to consent for other assignments; bars Garman from assigning to our competitors.
- § 3(c): conformed by cross-reference to Section 20(d) so the use restrictions do not undercut the new carve-out.

Fallback offered in the comment if Garman resists: mutual assignment to successors on written notice, with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
